'''Vicendi''' was a [[Historian/Legends|historian]] commissioned in [[10,000 BBY]] to create a list of [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] [[Wonders of the Galaxy/Legends|wonders]] for the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic's]] anniversary. His work, entitled the [[Twenty Wonders of the Galaxy]] and released in his ''[[Arturum Galactinum]]'', focused only on objects constructed by [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] beings. Vicendi's list was criticized by many who believed the historian had overemphasized both early Republic and [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] structures, and, in the [[Time/Legends|millennia]] that followed, various [[Species/Legends|species]] and groups compiled their own competing catalogs of wonders.

==Biography==
[[File:CaliusSajLeeloo-TLC1.jpg|thumb|right|280px|Vicendi included the crystal city of Calius saj Leeloo (pictured) in his list of the Twenty Wonders of the Galaxy.]]
Vicendi was a [[Historian/Legends|historian]] who lived around [[10,000 BBY]]. In that [[Standard year/Legends|year]], he compiled a list of [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] wonders for inclusion in his ''[[Arturum Galactinum]]'', a work commissioned to celebrate the anniversary of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. Vicendi opted to include only structures or objects constructed by [[Sentience/Legends|sentients]] into his list, disregarding natural wonders like the [[Corphelion Comets]] and the [[Fire Rings of Fornax]].<ref name="CSWE" /> He gathered a score of historical objects and locations&mdash;many of which were no longer in existence&mdash;into his final product, the [[Twenty Wonders of the Galaxy]]. The wonders Vicendi chose ranged from the towering, pre-Republic [[Statue of Xim]] to the [[Crystal/Legends|crystal]] [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Calius saj Leeloo]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Berchest/Legends|Berchest]], and from the fire-breathing [[Caliginous Automaton of Tomo-Reth]] to the massive [[Library/Legends|library]] on [[Obroa-skai/Legends|Obroa-skai]] known as the [[Celebratus Archive]].<ref name="Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref>

Many beings found fault with Vicendi's list, however, arguing that it was overly focused on wonders of the early Republic and placed too much emphasis on the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] region rather than the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]] as a whole. Over [[Time/Legends|time]], three [[Species/Legends|species]]&mdash;the [[Bothan/Legends|Bothans]], the [[Caamasi/Legends|Caamasi]], and the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutts]]&mdash;produced their own separate lists of galactic wonders. Millennia after Vicendi's lifetime, the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], in accordance with its [[High Human Culture/Legends|Human High Culture]] policies, rewrote the historian's list and distributed it through the [[Imperial Ministry of Education]] as "''[[Glorius Imperica]]''."<ref name="Atlas" />

==Personality and traits==
When crafting his list for ''Arturum Galactinum'', Vicendi disregarded natural wonders and instead focused solely on objects constructed by sentient beings. Critics of his Twenty Wonders of the Galaxy noted that the historian appeared to be biased toward the Core and the early history of the Republic.<ref name="Atlas" />

==Behind the scenes==
Vicendi was first mentioned in the "Twenty Wonders of the Galaxy" entry in ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'', a reference book published in [[2008]].<ref name="CSWE" />
